messages:
Support: heads up — multiple customers reporting 502/504s and timeouts since the 09:00 seed rollout. first alert from AcmeMaps ~09:12. seeing spike in gateway errors + tail latency.
Alex: oncall here. which rollout? seed-route prefetch_v2? any config flags flipped this morning?
Support: yes, rollout id seed-2026-03-17-09. config key 'route.split.prefetch_v2' set to true for 10% traffic at 09:00. ops dashboard shows 5xx rate jumped from 0.2% -> 8% over 15m.
Priya: I see increased 502s on the inference gateway. traces indicate upstream inference containers returning 500s while gateway reports 502. sampling: 60% of failing traces have KV cache miss + long serialization time.
Emily: customer impact: AcmeMaps and Travelly seeing elevated errors, some billing anomalies (requests retried) — CS already queued high-priority tickets.
Alex: can we get a short curl repro hitting the canary route? need a deterministic request shape.
Priya: sharing quick repro used on prod canary host:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "x-route: prefetch_v2" \
  -d '{"input":"repeat: test long prompt x100"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Priya: when I run that against canary we see 504 after ~10s and then backend logs show a memory spike at same time.
Claire: infra metric: GPU memory usage on canary pool nodes climbed to 98% during spike, OOM kill count 0 but retryable errors up. autoscaler didn't spin up extra because pool configured to fixed size for seed rollout.
Sam: Product note — prefetch_v2 was supposed to enable early KV prefetch + larger batch windows. maybe batch window is too big for this traffic pattern.
Alex: prioritize rollback if we suspect config. can we flip the flag to 0% for seed route? who has perms?
Support: I can coordinate. flipping to 0% now and notifying customers. ETA 2m.
OpsBot: deploybot: configuration change applied: route.split.prefetch_v2 -> 0% for rollout seed-2026-03-17-09 by Support at 09:25:14.
Priya: confirming — error rate dropping on gateway within one minute. still seeing some high latency tails for inflight requests.
Emily: sending update to affected customers: "we're rolling back a recent routing config which should reduce errors within minutes. we'll follow up with root cause." :thumbsup:
Sam: after rollback, we should run a controlled repro on a staging mirror to validate prefetch logic. also check batching window defaults and KV prefetch concurrency.
Alex: action items:
- Priya + Claire: collect kernel/pod logs for the canary pool, memory profiles (heap + native) — tag timeframe 09:00-09:30
- Emily: collate affected customer request ids for billing reconciliation
- Sam: schedule a canary postmortem with eng-runtime next week
- Support: coordinate final rollback confirmation and close CS tickets
Priya: quick snippet of backend error from canary logs:
```
2026-03-17T09:13:22Z ERROR runtime::model ServeError("tokenizer out-of-memory while serializing logits") tid=0x7f
trace_id=abc123 client=acct-acmemaps request_id=req_98765
```
Claire: infra note: we disabled burst autoscale for seed rollout to keep metrics stable. that likely blocked cushion for unexpected memory overhead.
Alex: agreed. incident severity: P1 until all customers back to baseline. moving to incident channel for cross-team follow-ups.
Support: baseline metrics show 5xx back to <0.4% after rollback, tail latency returning to normal. will keep monitoring for 60m and update.
Emily: closing loop: CS notify sent, billing flagged for manual review — will avoid automatic credits until we confirm retry amplification.
Sam: postmortem owners: Priya (root cause), Claire (infra config), Alex (rollback timeline), Emily (customer comms). I'll draft initial timeline.
Priya: next steps for runtime: add guardrails so prefetch_v2 fails closed when mem pressure detected, and add a canary policy that preserves autoscale for small seed pools.
Alex: thanks everyone. please paste collected logs and the final timeline into the incident doc after 60m.
Support: noted. leaving thread open until 10:30 for final signoff. :white_check_mark:
